identity.name: Liberia
alt_names: American Colonization Society settlement at Cape Mesurado

capitals.name: Monrovia
capitals.note: The settlement at Cape Mesurado is the later Monrovia; the History of Liberia page says that when the Commonwealth was formed (1838/1839) 'Monrovia was named the capital'. The Liberia page names Monrovia as 'the capital and largest city'. Coordinates are the gazetteer's.

correction.text: Cape Mesurado, 'a 36-mile-long (58 km) strip of land near present-day Monrovia', acquired by the American Colonization Society in December 1821

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Liberia row before 1848 and draws the settlement inside its United States of America rows (1822: 29 cells, about 7,300 km2; 1824-27: 93 cells; 1828-33: 192; 1834-39: 284; 1840-47: 501 cells), which the US dossier removes. The page gives only the Cape Mesurado strip for the first settlement and names five further colonies created 'until 1835' without extents or places, so the core is a 40 km radius round Monrovia (11 cells, about 2,800 km2); growth along the coast before 1842 is not drawn because no opened page places it.

correction.text: 'By 1842, four out of the aforementioned five colonies were incorporated into Liberia'; the Republic of Maryland stayed separate, so Liberia's claimed domain without Maryland

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Commonwealth 1842-1846, Republic from 26 July 1847). The pages give no extent for the merged colonies; the outline is Cliopatria's 1848 Liberia shape without Maryland County, the same land its United States rows drew for 1840-47 (501 cells against 526 for the 1848 shape). Treat as a claimed domain with soft edges, not as governed land; unverified beyond the page's list of colonies.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1848 shape without Maryland County, which was the separate Republic of Maryland until 18 March 1857; holds for 1848-1856, and from 1857 the shape stands (see republic-of-liberia_1857)

keyframe_review.note: 101,997 km2 against the infobox's 111,370 km2 (no year given; ratio 0.92), so the area is fine. Infobox: 'Republic of Maryland annexed: March 18, 1857'; the shape includes Maryland County (14 cells, about 3,500 km2) from 1848. The History of Liberia page dates the Grebo and Kru insurgency that forced Maryland into Liberia to 1854 and the border pages say 1857; the infobox date is used. The shape's fringe in Guinea (lat 7.4-8.5, lon -10.3 to -8.5) and Ivory Coast (east of the Cavalla) is claimed hinterland that the 1892 and 1907 French treaties removed; the History page says Liberia's expansion 'brought the colony into border disputes with the French and British'.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1848 shape unchanged once the Republic of Maryland is annexed on 18 March 1857

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe that gives Cliopatria's 1848 outline back to Liberia from 1857, after the Maryland correction ends; the shape itself is unchanged. The page does not describe any other territorial change before the treaties of 1885-1892.

correction.text: The 1848 outline holds through 1892: Cliopatria drops a 10-cell fringe in the north (Guinea side, about 2,500 km2) in 1885, but no opened page puts a French frontier before the treaty of 8 December 1892; the Anglo-Liberian treaty of 11 November 1885 is on the Mano river, whose side the shape already follows

keyframe_review.note: 100,596 km2 against the infobox's 111,370 km2 (ratio 0.90). The Guinea-Liberia page: 'France and Liberia signed a boundary treaty on 8 December 1892' (straight lines, north of the present line); the Liberia-Sierra Leone page: 'an Anglo-Liberian boundary treaty was signed on 11 November 1885, which utilised the Mano river as the boundary', but names no land. Cliopatria's 1885 step therefore has no dated page behind it; the correction keeps the 1848 outline for 1885-1892 and the new keyframes below carry 1893 onward. The shape's remaining years (1893-1894) are replaced by republic-of-liberia_1893.

correction.text: After the Franco-Liberian treaty of 8 December 1892 the frontier follows 'the Cavalla River and a series of straight lines' in the east and lies 'north of the current line' in the north: the 1895 outline (modern Liberia) plus the northern fringe that the 1848 outline has and the 1885 outline lacks

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Ivory Coast page: the 1892 boundary 'used the Cavalla River and a series of straight lines'; the Guinea page: the 1892 line was 'north of the current line' until the treaty of 18 September 1907 moved it south. Neither page gives coordinates or the area of the strip, so the strip is Cliopatria's own fringe (10 cells, 2,529 km2): an approximation at confidence 2. Cliopatria's 1895 shape (modern Liberia) is therefore too small for 1895-1906.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe at confidence 1 for the Parrot's Beak: the Liberia-Sierra Leone page says the Mano boundary 'was then extended further northwards by mutual agreement in June 1903' and that in January 1911 'Liberia ceded the Parrot's Beak area to Sierra Leone', but it does not say that the 1903 agreement gave the Beak to Liberia or when Liberia first held it. The region name is not yet in the gazetteer.

Guinea-Liberia page: 'on 18 September 1907, confirmed in January 1911', the boundary was moved south 'to its present position'; the Sierra Leone page adds that the French treaty 'resulted in Liberia ceding a sizeable strip of territory to France'. From 1907 the north frontier is the modern line, which is what Cliopatria's 1895 shape draws.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1895 shape (modern Liberia) unchanged but valid only for 1911-1941; for 1895-1910 use republic-of-liberia_1893, _1903 and _1907

keyframe_review.note: 99,563 km2 against the infobox's 111,370 km2 (ratio 0.89). A verdict on years only: the shape is the present-day border, which the Sierra Leone page says was reached in January 1911 ('Britain and Liberia further modified the boundary in January 1911'), the French line having been moved to it on 18 September 1907; demarcation ran 1926-1929 in the north, 1913-14 (agreed 1917) with Sierra Leone, and 'small adjustments' were approved in January 1930. The 1930 adjustments are not drawn.

99,563 km2 against the infobox's 111,370 km2 (ratio 0.89, within the factor of two; the infobox gives no year). The border is the post-1930 line; nothing on the page changes it to 2023.
Same outline as 1943-2023; the infobox's 111,370 km2 is the current area. Unchanged.

region.text: Cape Mesurado, 'a 36-mile-long (58 km) strip of land near present-day Monrovia'

ledger.note: 1822: American Colonization Society settlers found Liberia at Cape Mesurado. Infobox: 'American Colonization Society settlement: January 7, 1822'. The History of Liberia page (second page) says 'In December 1821, they acquired Cape Mesurado' from King Peter, 'a 36-mile-long (58 km) strip of land near present-day Monrovia'; the 40 km radius is my reading. The land belonged to local rulers, not a state, hence nobody; the US government 'declined to act upon requests from the ACS to make Liberia an American colony or to establish a formal protectorate' (History page), so the US dossier's Liberia cells are not US land.

1839: the settlements are reorganised as the Commonwealth of Liberia, with Monrovia as capital. History of Liberia: 'In 1839, it was reorganized into the Commonwealth of Liberia' and 'Monrovia was named the capital'; the same page also says 'In 1838 the former four settlements came together to create the Commonwealth of Liberia'. Liberia page: the oldest counties were 'both founded in 1839 prior to Liberian independence'. The colour and dossier continue.

region.text: 'four out of the aforementioned five colonies were incorporated into Liberia'; Liberia's claimed domain without Maryland

ledger.counterpart: the other colonization societies' colonies (Kentucky-in-Africa, Mississippi in Africa, Louisiana and Pennsylvania settlements)
ledger.note: By 1842: the settlements of the other state colonization societies are merged into Liberia. 'Until 1835, five more colonies were created by the colonization societies of five different states'; 'By 1842, four out of the aforementioned five colonies were incorporated into Liberia'; the Pennsylvania settlement Port Cresson 'was destroyed by indigenous people'. The page's own list of five names Maryland among them and so does not say which four merged or in which year; the date is an upper bound and the region is Cliopatria's 1848 outline without Maryland, a bridging reading.

1847, 26 July: Liberia declares its independence as a republic. Infobox 'Independence declared: July 26, 1847'; History of Liberia: 'On July 26, 1847, eleven signatories' established 'the free and independent Republic of Liberia'. Britain recognised it in 1848, France in 1852, the United States in 1862 (History page). Colour and dossier continue.

1857, 18 March: Liberia annexes the Republic of Maryland. Infobox 'Republic of Maryland annexed: March 18, 1857'; the Ivory Coast and Sierra Leone border pages also say Maryland joined in 1857. The History of Liberia page says Maryland 'was forced by an insurgency of the Grebo and the Kru people to join Liberia' and dates it to 1854. Maryland County is my reading of the republic's extent.

region.text: the outline east of the Cavalla River, where the treaty set the boundary on 'the Cavalla River and a series of straight lines'

ledger.note: 1892, 8 December: the Franco-Liberian treaty fixes the frontier with French Ivory Coast on the Cavalla River. 'France and Liberia signed a treaty on 8 December 1892 outlining a boundary between Liberian and French territory'; it 'used the Cavalla River and a series of straight lines'. The page does not say what land Liberia gave up; the region is the 7 cells (about 1,770 km2) that Cliopatria's 1885 outline has east of the river and its 1895 outline lacks. Cliopatria dates the step to 1895.

region.text: the Parrot's Beak area, later Sierra Leone

ledger.note: 1903, June: the Anglo-Liberian boundary is extended northwards, apparently giving Liberia the Parrot's Beak area. Page: 'this was then extended further northwards by mutual agreement in June 1903'; the page is silent on who held the Beak before and on what the extension gave, and the gain is inferred from the 1911 cession of 'the Parrot's Beak area' by Liberia.

region.text: the northern fringe the 1892 line left Liberia, 'a sizeable strip of territory' ceded to France when the frontier 'moved southwards to its current position'

ledger.note: 1907, 18 September: a second Franco-Liberian treaty moves the northern frontier south to its present line. 'another treaty on 18 September 1907 (confirmed in January 1911) which moved it southwards to its current position' (Ivory Coast page); the Sierra Leone page says the French treaty 'resulted in Liberia ceding a sizeable strip of territory to France'. The strip is drawn as Cliopatria's 10-cell fringe in Guinea (2,529 km2), the only outline available; Cliopatria dates its loss to 1885.

region.text: the Parrot's Beak area, later Sierra Leone

ledger.note: 1911, January: Liberia cedes the Parrot's Beak area to Sierra Leone. 'Britain and Liberia further modified the boundary in January 1911'; Liberia ceded the Parrot's Beak 'in exchange for territory east of the Mano river'. The page gives no extent for the land received, so no gain is drawn for it.

1980, 12 April: Master Sergeant Samuel Doe's coup overthrows and kills President Tolbert. Page: 'On April 12, 1980, a military coup led by Master Sergeant Samuel Doe of the Krahn ethnic group overthrew and killed President William R. Tolbert Jr.' Regime change in the same state; no border moves.

wars.name: Grebo and Kru insurgency against the Republic of Maryland

zones.text: the Republic of Maryland, which joined Liberia

wars.outcome: The Republic of Maryland 'was forced by an insurgency of the Grebo and the Kru people to join Liberia'; the Liberian infobox gives the annexation as 18 March 1857.
wars.note: The History of Liberia page places the insurgency and the joining in 1854; the Liberia infobox and both border pages say 1857. The page does not say that Liberia fought. The years run from the page's 1854 to the annexation.

wars.name: First Liberian Civil War
wars.outcome: A rebel group 'launched an insurrection in December 1989 against Doe's government'; 'By September 1990, Doe's forces controlled only a small area' and Doe was captured and executed that month; Charles Taylor was elected president in 1997.
wars.note: No territorial result on the page: it names no zone held by the rebels, so no contest or rebel-state events are drawn. A gap-filler should read the war's own article for the rebel-held areas.

wars.name: Second Liberian Civil War
wars.outcome: Taylor resigned in August 2003 and went into exile in Nigeria; the 2005 elections followed.
wars.note: The Liberia page dates the start to 1998 in its introduction and to 1999 in a later section. No zones named.

certainty.note: Coastal settlements with a claimed hinterland, Cape Mesurado was acquired from King Peter (History of Liberia); no survey or treaty frontier with a European power. The border with the Republic of Maryland (to 1857) is a coastal boundary between settlements.

The Sierra Leone frontier is on the Mano river from the treaty of 11 November 1885 and was extended north in June 1903; the French frontier is treaty straight lines from 8 December 1892, moved south on 18 September 1907, but none is demarcated until 1913-1929.

Treaty lines: the Sierra Leone boundary modified in January 1911, demarcated 1913-14, confirmed 1917 and adjusted by treaty in January 1930; the French (Guinea and Ivory Coast) boundary of 1907, confirmed January 1911 and demarcated 1926-1929, accepted by Ivory Coast in 1961 and Guinea in 1960.

sources.title: Liberia-Sierra Leone border

notes:
Group af-04-b, one state. Page budget: up to 5 pages for 6 Cliopatria shapes; all 5 opened (Liberia, History of Liberia, the Ivory Coast-Liberia, Guinea-Liberia and Liberia-Sierra Leone border pages). Quotes in notes are the WebFetch extractor's rendering of the dated sentence, close paraphrase rather than byte-exact.

DECISION: the dossier starts in 1822, not at Cliopatria's 1848. Cliopatria has no Liberia row before 1848 and draws the colony inside its United States of America rows 1822-1847 (29 cells in 1822 growing to 501 by 1840); the US dossier (am-07-c) removes those cells because the History of Liberia page says the US 'declined to act upon requests from the ACS to make Liberia an American colony', so without this dossier the land would be nobody's for 26 years. Four new keyframes cover 1822-1856 (1822, 1842, with 1848 and 1857 around the Maryland correction). If the orchestrator prefers a sovereign-state start, the 1822 and 1839 events and the first two keyframes can be dropped and the found event moved to 26 July 1847.

CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO CORRECT: (1) 1848-1884 includes Maryland County (Republic of Maryland until 18 March 1857). (2) The 1885 step drops a 10-cell northern fringe (Guinea side, 2,529 km2) with no page behind it; the pages put the French line at 8 December 1892 (north of the present line) and its move south on 18 September 1907, so the fringe is kept to 1906 and the Ivory Coast cells east of the Cavalla (7 cells, 1,770 km2) leave in 1892, not 1895. (3) The 1895-1941 shape is the present border and omits the Parrot's Beak area that Liberia held until January 1911 (confidence 1 on when it was gained). (4) The 1942 shape is a three-cell artefact. The fringe and Beak geometries are approximations: no page gives coordinates, so the strip ceded to France is drawn as Cliopatria's own fringe.

NOT SETTLED: the extent of Liberia's settled land 1822-1884 (no opened page gives one; the 1842 and 1848 outlines are claimed domains); the date and size of the 1885 Anglo-Liberian cession (the page says only that the Mano river was used as the boundary); the 1911 territory 'east of the Mano river' received in exchange; Gallinas and the 1906 agreement (not on the Sierra Leone page); the 1930 adjustments; Maryland's date of independence (not on any page opened; the Maryland insurgency is 1854 on the History page, 1857 elsewhere); which four of the five colonies merged by 1842. NPFL or other rebel-held land in the 1989-1997 war and the 2000s: the Liberia page names no zones, so no rebel dossier or contest events are written.

NEEDS A DOSSIER FROM ANOTHER GROUP: Republic of Maryland (slug republic-of-maryland, annexed by Liberia on 18 March 1857 per the Liberia infobox; counterpart of the 1857 gain; its own start date is on no page opened). Counterparts used by slug: british-africa and french-africa (af-08). Region names the gazetteer lacks: Parrot's Beak (a salient of Kailahun District, Sierra Leone, between Liberia and Guinea). The Mano and Cavalla (Cavally) rivers are not in the gazetteer's rivers and are not used as regions.

Rulers omitted: the pages opened name presidents only in passing (Tubman 1944, Tolbert, Doe, Taylor 1997, Sirleaf 2005-2018, Weah 2018, Boakai 2024) and give no complete list with reign years.
